import json
q=json.load(open('drafts/quiz-0002.json')); k=json.load(open('drafts/key-0002.json'))
I={i['id']:i for i in q['items']}; K={i['id']:i for i in k['items']}
I['q1']['options']=[
 {"id":"a","text":"Agents call tools to get information, and workflows never do"},
 {"id":"b","text":"An agent's tools run inside the model, while a workflow's tools run in the program"},
 {"id":"c","text":"In a workflow, code fixes the order of steps; in an agent, the model decides the next step"},
 {"id":"d","text":"One model call per request makes a workflow, and several calls make an agent"}]
I['q3']['stem']="An agent keeps calling the model until it decides to stop, while a fixed workflow makes a set number of calls. What does an agent therefore do more of, which makes each request cost more? Answer in a few words."
K['q3']['answer']="model calls"
K['q3']['accepted']=["more model calls","calls to the model","model calls per request","calls","tokens","it makes more model calls","extra model calls","steps"]
K['q3']['rationale']="An agent loops until it decides to stop, so a request takes more model calls, and how many is not known in advance; a workflow has a fixed, small number. An answer about the agent using a bigger or smarter model misses that the extra cost comes from the loop."
I['q4']['options'][2]={"id":"c","text":"An agent's output varies from run to run, so it cannot be tested at all"}
K['q4']['rationale']=K['q4']['rationale'].replace("the belief that an agent cannot be inspected or tested","the belief that an agent cannot be tested at all because its output varies")
I['q5']['stem']="Each evening the assistant reminds every student who has a booking tomorrow. It does this in three steps:\n- Look up tomorrow's bookings.\n- Write one friendly message per booking.\n- Send each message.\nNo student is involved while it runs. Which design is the cheapest and most predictable?"
I['q5']['options'][1]={"id":"b","text":"An agent, because deciding when to send needs judgment, so the model must decide it"}
I['q5']['options'][2]={"id":"c","text":"A workflow, because every night follows the same known steps, and code can loop over the bookings"}
K['q5']['rationale']=K['q5']['rationale'].replace("b shows M11, that acting through tools makes a system an agent","b shows M20, that any step needing judgment means the model must own the control flow")
K['q5']['distractors']['b']="M20"
I['q6']['stem']="A student asks:\n\"I want to cut a 6 mm acrylic case with a hinge. Which machine should I use, do I need training, and when can I get time?\"\nWhich tools are needed, and in what order, depends on what each answer turns up. The possible combinations are too many to write out. Which design is best for handling requests like this within a small budget?"
I['q6']['options'][1]={"id":"b","text":"Let the model pick which tool to use next, with a limit on how long it can work so cost stays bounded"}
I['q6']['options'][3]={"id":"d","text":"Let the model keep working until it says it is done, because a limit could cut answers short"}

json.dump(q,open('quizzes/0002.json','w'),indent=2)
json.dump(k,open('keys/0002.json','w'),indent=2)
EOF

Quiz 0002 is written at `quizzes/0002.json`, with its key at `keys/0002.json`.

It has six questions on O4, "Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow". Four check the core ideas and two apply them to makerspace situations:
- **Core ideas:** who owns the control flow (code in a workflow, the model in an agent), and why using tools or several model calls doesn't make something an agent. It also covers why agents cost more per request, and why a fixed workflow is easier to test.
- **Applying:** a nightly booking-reminder job, and an open-ended student request with a small budget.

- **Ahead of the lessons:** there is no lesson on this objective yet, so the quiz is ahead of the lessons. The cost and testing questions rely on ideas Riley hasn't been taught, and I made the cost question's stem supply its premise.
- **Misconception ids:** I couldn't read `keys/0001.json`, so I used M11–M22 for the misconceptions in this key. If quiz 0001's key already uses any of those ids for something else, they will need renumbering.
- **Reviews:** both review passes ran, and the second one still had 8 findings. I fixed most of them and left a few on purpose. For example, I did not reorder the items, because the item ids stay stable. The review record is `review-records/0002-quiz.md`.

Riley can take it when they are ready.
